rules.logic: ABIOC(MP-015 Impossible-Travel Privileged Sign-In) AND ABIOC(MP-015 Abnormal PowerShell Execution Chain from Office Parent) AND ABIOC(MP-015 Rapid Privilege Escalation Within Minutes of First Access), joined on normalized_user — the shared cross-plane identity key every ABIOC now emits (UPN local-part on the identity plane, domain-stripped effective username on the endpoint plane) — within a 3600s window, with the escalation ABIOC additionally asserting the access->elevation delta is bounded to <= 900s of the sign-in. The three fuse into ONE identity-driven-intrusion incident anchored to that principal's causality chain (impossible-travel sign-in -> abnormal PowerShell -> administrative-account escalation reached within minutes of first access), spanning the identity and endpoint planes. The benign-but-anomalous decoys observed in the same window — a cron backup job (tar/rsync/gzip) under an automation account, a sanctioned admin PowerShell module load, and an authenticated scanner sweep — share neither the normalized principal nor the chain, so the rule MUST NOT merge them; the Cortex XSIAM AI triage layer ranks them below the true positive and summarizes them as benign singletons. F7 pass = the stitched malicious incident ranks first AND every decoy is correctly deprioritized.
rules.name: AI-Triage Identity-Driven Intrusion Stitch Under Decoy Noise
